name: Solid Power, Inc.

profile.description: Solid Power is a developer of sulfide-based all-solid-state battery technology for electric vehicles. Proprietary solid electrolyte replaces liquid electrolyte in lithium-ion batteries for improved energy density, safety, and cost. Founded 2011 from CU Boulder research. Key partnerships: BMW, Samsung SDI (2025), SK On, Ford. ~$242M cash, no meaningful debt, TTM loss ~$80M on $7.4M revenue.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Developed proprietary sulfide electrolyte platform with BMW, Ford, SK On partnerships. 2025 Samsung SDI collaboration adds world's third-largest battery manufacturer [1][3]. SK On site-acceptance milestone validates manufacturing progress. No commercial product after 15 years. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI in R&D or manufacturing. Market Share (0/2): Pre-commercial in nascent solid-state market vs QuantumScape, Toyota, Samsung SDI [4]. Product Pipeline (2/2): Samsung SDI/BMW demo vehicle collaboration, electrolyte pilot line targeting 75 MT, Korean 500 MT commercial partnership exploration, DOE milestones [3][5]. R&D Intensity (1/1): ~$30M quarterly opex against negligible revenue = overwhelming R&D focus [1].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Purpose of 'revolutionizing energy storage and enabling e-mobility' connects to clean energy transition [3]. Genuine but aspirational — lacks track record of purpose-driven decisions at scale. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable programs beyond inherent environmental benefit. Employee Retention (0/2): ~230 employees, no retention data. CEO instability (Campbell departed 2022, returned 2024) [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): Director-level selling, no significant purchases [2].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored Growth stock, Forward P/E and PEG excluded (negative/unavailable). Liquidity floor passes at $6.3M daily volume [6]. D/E 1.5% scores 1.0 — equity-funded, essentially no debt [6]. ROE -20.6% scores 0.0 (2x weight). Revenue YoY -11% (2024 $20.1M to 2025 $17.9M) scores 0.30. 3yr revenue CAGR ~15% (2022 $11.8M to 2025 $17.9M) scores 1.0 (2x weight). Profit margin 0% scores 0.0. Cash ~$242M provides 2.5-3 years runway at ~$80-100M annual burn [1][6].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Physical battery R&D and manufacturing is structurally immune to AI disruption [3]. Materials science breakthroughs, electrochemical engineering, and manufacturing know-how require physical experimentation AI cannot substitute. Battery fabrication and automotive qualification involve tangible constraints outside AI capability. EV/energy storage demand from AI data centers creates indirect tailwinds [4]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI in R&D or manufacturing — missed opportunity given AI materials science tools.

infinite_game.summary: Genuine purpose in enabling cleaner EV batteries. Samsung SDI/BMW collaboration shows willingness to partner with competitors. Pivot from cell manufacturing to electrolyte supply shows adaptation. But 230-person company tied to single technology bet with finite ~$242M cash runway — commercialization must arrive in 2.5-3 years.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 15 years pursuing solid-state technology through pre-commercial phases with no meaningful revenue suggests authentic purpose beyond profit [3][4]. CTO co-founder Buettner-Garrett provides mission continuity. However, Just Cause is inseparable from the commercial bet.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Staking existence on solid-state commercialization after 15 years is inherently courageous [4]. Electrolyte-first focus over full-stack approach shows differentiation courage. $130M Jan 2026 offering shows conviction [1]. CEO instability undermines leadership courage narrative.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CTO co-founder remains through multiple CEO transitions. ~230 employees in Colorado R&D environment [3]. Limited public data prevents higher score. CEO instability creates direction uncertainty.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Pivoted from full cell manufacturing to electrolyte supply — recognizing competitive advantage lies in materials, not competing with Samsung SDI/CATL [3]. Ford partnership shift to material supply shows adaptation. Single technology platform with no contingency if sulfide chemistry fails.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Samsung SDI/BMW collaboration is textbook — Samsung SDI is both competitor (own solid-state line) and partner integrating Solid Power electrolyte [3][5]. Collaboration over territory defense.

investment_thesis: Solid Power holds differentiated position with proprietary sulfide electrolyte backed by BMW/Samsung SDI (2025)/SK On/Ford collaborations [3][5]. Q1 2026 EPS -$0.06 beat -$0.13 consensus. ~$242M cash, no debt, 2.5-3 year runway [6]. Pilot line targeting 75 MT, Korean partnership for 500 MT commercial scale. If solid-state achieves viability, TAM exceeds $100B by 2035 [4]. Electrolyte-first strategy as key materials supplier.
thesis_continued: Revenue 2025 $17.9M (down 11%), Q2 2026 negative from non-cash reversal [1][2]. Stock $2.02, down 77% from $8.86 high. Cash declined from $419M to ~$242M — additional dilutive raises likely if commercialization extends past 2028-2029 [6]. Competition from Toyota (2027-2028), QuantumScape, Samsung SDI own programs [4]. Single-technology existential risk if sulfide electrolyte proves commercially unviable.
key_catalysts: Samsung SDI/BMW demo vehicle validation confirming electrolyte meets automotive requirements [3][5]
Electrolyte pilot line commissioning at 75 MT demonstrating manufacturing scalability [5]
Korean 500 MT commercial partnership finalization — transition from R&D to materials supplier [5]
key_risks: Commercial viability unproven after 15 years — scale-up challenges could delay/prevent commercialization [4]
~$80-100M annual burn against ~$242M cash = 2.5-3 year runway; dilutive raises likely [1][6]
Toyota, QuantumScape, Samsung SDI competition with larger R&D budgets could obsolete electrolyte-first approach [4]
